addendum: Wikipedia-led tests, addendum j: a combined alert list (library, Wikipedia, event calendar, sales lists, and book-linked Wikipedia pages of every kind)
parent_record: prereg/wiki_led_settings_2026-10-20.json, addenda a to i; their settings apply unless changed here
fixed_by: Claude, for Khant Phyo Wai, who asked on 22 Oct (about 05:35) for the combined alert-list test now, with Wikipedia pages categorised more intelligently than films and adaptations only: history, events and many more
units: Test A's 7,747 works and their corrected rows (data/db/wiki_led/test_a_rows_c.parquet), Test A's training and test years, walk-forward refits by test year, seed 20261020.
book_links: For each work's Wikidata item, the linked items and their English Wikipedia pages, by link type: subject (P921 main subject, P180 depicts), event or period (P2408 set in period, and subject items that are occurrences), place (P840 narrative location), character (P674), person (subject items that are humans), adaptation (P144 reverse and P4969), series (P179, the other books of the series). The author (P50) stays in the W features as in Test A. Category of each linked page: event or history, person, place, work, concept or other, from Wikidata P31 and its classes (occurrence Q1190554 and subclasses = event; human Q5 = person; geographic location = place; creative work = work); where the page was sorted in Test F, the AI's page kind is kept beside it. Wikidata SPARQL with at least 1.5 s between queries, cached.
linked_page_attention: Full daily user views (Wikimedia REST, all-access, user, 2015-07-01 to 2026-09-30, at most 3 requests a second, one downloader at a time; pages already in the Test F store reused) for linked pages, at most 30,000 pages, by link type in the order adaptation, subject, event or period, person, place, character, series. Per page and month: a burst when the month's views reach 3 times the median of the 6 months before and at least 3,000 views, or when the page is in the daily top 500 on any day of the month.
scheduled_calendar: Known in advance at month t, for months t+1 to t+3: film or television adaptation releases (D2), round anniversaries (a multiple of 25 years) of linked dated events (P585, P580 with month precision) and of the author's birth and death (P569, P570); and, known in month t: the author's death in month t (D2).
sales: From D3's monthly NYT table: on any list in month t, entered a list in month t, weeks on lists in month t.
features: H = Test A's library history; W = Test A's corrected Wikipedia features; E = the scheduled calendar; N = the NYT features; L = book-linked page bursts in month t and t-1, by link type and by category (counts and any).
models: LightGBM with Test A's settings, no tuning, fitted per test year on earlier years; ladder H, H+W, H+W+E, H+W+E+N, H+W+E+N+L (the full model). Placebo: E and L built with all dates moved 12 months earlier, in the full model.
targets: Surge next month: L_next at least 2 times M6 and at least 5 loans more than M6; also a surge in months t+1 to t+3 (the largest of the three months), with the models refitted on that target.
measures: Per origin month: the share of the top 20 that surge (precision at 20), among all works and among works not yet risen at t (L_t below 1.5 times M6); average precision; coverage = share of all surges found in the top 100. Means over months with month-block bootstrap intervals (blocks of 3 months, 2,000 draws), paired for differences.
decision: Primary: precision at 20 for next-month surges among works not yet risen, full model minus H: interval above 0. Secondary: every step of the ladder, the 3-month target, all works, coverage, the placebo (the full model's gain over H must exceed the placebo model's gain for the event information to count), and each category of linked pages added alone to H+W.
time_rule: Results reported on 22 Oct 2026 by 20:00 +07; if the linked-page views are not complete by 15:00, L is built from the pages stored by then and the coverage is reported.
seen_before_fixing: All results of Tests A to F, addenda h and i (D1 to D3), including D2's not-yet-risen comparison (added after D2's first run) which suggested the not-yet-risen measure here, and the improvement round v2 (events as features gave no gain over dates moved 12 months). No result of this combined test exists.
